Perhaps it would be better if the course didn't require students to choose a book from two lists of resources. I'm sure most students don't read the book they choose from the required list, so maybe in a place like a university, helping students show themselves in unexpected areas is better than forcing them to find what suits them from lists that you've limited them to. At a university like Bilkent, unexpected perspectives and experiences can emerge from unexpected fields; instead of preventing this, students should be helped to find these areas. And the Turkish language course is one of the limited areas where they can demonstrate this, and they shouldn't be prevented from doing so.
